claim.claim-text: 1. A method for reducing beverage loss during loading of beverage into an ethanol concentration system, the ethanol concentration system having a set of reverse osmosis pressure vessels, each pressure vessel having a feed inlet, a retentate outlet, and a permeate outlet, the pressure vessels being coupled so that each successive pressure vessel has its feed inlet coupled to the retentate outlet of its preceding pressure vessel, the method comprising:

2. A method according to claim 1, further comprising obtaining the retentate from the retentate outlet of the second pressure vessel when the alcohol percentage is in a second target range, the second target range different from the first target range.
3. A method according to claim 2, wherein the second target range is 15-25% ABV for a beer beverage.
4. A method according to any one of claims 2-3, wherein the obtaining includes directing the retentate to a product tank coupled to the retentate outlet of the second pressure vessel.
5. A method according to any one of claims 1 to 4, wherein monitoring includes using one or more sensors to determine the alcohol percentage and/or a real extract percentage.

6. A method according to claim 5, wherein the one or more sensors include an inline sound velocity sensor, an inline refractive index sensor, an inline near infrared sensor, and/or an inline density sensor.
7. A method according to claim 5 or 6, wherein monitoring further includes using a thermocouple.

8. A method for reducing beverage loss during loading of beverage into an ethanol concentration system, the ethanol concentration system having a set of reverse osmosis pressure vessels, each pressure vessel having a feed inlet, a retentate outlet, and a permeate outlet, the pressure vessels being coupled so that each successive pressure vessel has its feed inlet coupled to the retentate outlet of its preceding pressure vessel, the method comprising:

9. A method according to claim 8, further comprising pressurizing the ethanol concentration system to within a pressure range of 1500 psi to 3000 psi while blocking the portion of the retentate outlet of the second pressure vessel.
10. A method according to claim 9, further comprising, after pressurizing the ethanol concentration system to within the pressure range, unblocking the retentate outlet and obtaining the retentate.

11. A method for reducing beverage loss during unloading of beverage out of an ethanol concentration system, the ethanol concentration system having a set of reverse osmosis pressure vessels, each pressure vessel having a feed inlet, a retentate outlet, and a permeate outlet, the pressure vessels being coupled so that each successive pressure vessel has its feed inlet coupled to the retentate outlet of its preceding pressure vessel, the method comprising:
12. An ethanol concentration system for reducing beverage loss during loading or unloading of a beverage into or from the ethanol concentration system, the ethanol concentration system comprising:

13. An ethanol concentration system according to claim 12, wherein the one or more sensors include an inline sound velocity sensor, an inline refractive index sensor, an inline near infrared sensor, and/or an inline density sensor.

14. A method for reducing beverage loss during loading of beverage into a water removal system, the water removal system having a set of reverse osmosis pressure vessels, each pressure vessel having a feed inlet, a retentate outlet, and a permeate outlet, the pressure vessels being coupled so that each successive pressure vessel has its feed inlet coupled to the retentate outlet of its preceding pressure vessel, the method comprising:
